name: Frappe HR v16 to the Norn canon

correspondences.justification: A Frappe HR Employee is a natural-person Agent; Norn keeps active employment terms on separate hr.Employment records linked to core.Agent.
A Frappe HR Department is a hierarchical organizational unit (org.OrgUnit).
A Frappe HR Designation maps onto a budgeted role/position (org.Post).
A Frappe HR Branch is a site/location organizational unit (org.OrgUnit); security scoping still binds to identity.BusinessUnit.
An Employee Group acts as a team/roster grouping specialized under org.OrgUnit.
A Holiday List acts as an operating calendar; Norn's time.Calendar also pins IANA tzdb and DST rules.
Each holiday or weekly-off date row is a calendar exception attached to a calendar.
A Leave Allocation grants days into a conserved employee leave balance.
A Leave Application is an employee leave request over a date interval.
A Shift Type defines a recurring local wall-clock operating window materialized to UTC intervals.
A Shift Assignment is a promised labor commitment assigned to an employee.
Posted Attendance records actual work fulfilling a shift commitment.
Newly allocated leave days are a conserved resource quantity in UCUM days.
Total allocated leave days including carry-forward are a conserved leave quantity in UCUM days.
Signed leave days credited or debited on a Leave Ledger Entry represent a conserved leave quantity in UCUM days.
Encashed leave days debited from leave balance are a conserved leave quantity in UCUM days.
Submitting an approved Leave Application debits the leave ledger; Norn enforces independent-approver authority.
Both refuse leave exceeding available balance; Norn never permits silent negative-balance bypass without an explicit policy.
Refuses overlapping leave intervals for the same employee.
Refusing self-approval on Leave Applications is a specialization of Norn's independent-approver law across leave, roster, and financial actions.
Refuses overlapping scheduled shifts for the same employee.
Refusing self-approval on Expense Claims is a specialization of Norn's independent-approver law (#618).
